current_bottleneck: The current best remains 377a at 8/11. Naive learned conditional base-noise scaling reduces FM loss but degrades calibrated scenario quality, showing that learned conditional priors need a likelihood-correct or otherwise constrained objective.
last_result_summary: 384a added an optional conditional diagonal noise-scale head to the empirical normal-score causal-memory transition FM and enabled it during recent adaptation. The scale head shrank average base-noise scale from 1.0 to about 0.75 and reduced adaptation loss to 0.263, but official score fell to 6/11. It failed coverage, conditionality, regime_coverage, distributional_fidelity, and mean_reversion. Daily KS improved to 25/25, but level KS collapsed to 3/25 and overall 90% coverage fell to 86.7%.
next_step_recommendation: Do not pursue naive learned base-prior scaling without a proper objective. The next principled move is data-framing rather than another architecture knob: test rolling/recent empirical normal-score quantiles for adaptation and decoding, because the stable failure is level occupancy under nonstationary validation marginals while daily transition shape is already good.
